round_27_fixes_checked.1 empty drum ring: landed: the ring is now a lawn with private patios, tables, planters and play corners per unit; no empty tile band.
round_27_fixes_checked.2 executive richer: landed partly: wood floors throughout, a lounge with sofa and media wall, a proper desk; still the same furniture family as Family, so the premium read comes mostly from floor colour and space.
round_27_fixes_checked.3 night: partly: lamps glow at beds and tables, but rooms are still dim grey away from the lamps (residence_tube_l_night).
round_27_fixes_checked.4 vault exterior: landed: seam lines, porch lamps, and the Executive ribbon glazing reads.
round_27_fixes_checked.5 Family vs Executive at 250 m: landed: the Executive terrace (wood deck, loungers, pergola) reads; at night the Executive vault shows more lit windows.
round_27_fixes_checked.6 children's rooms: landed: bunks with colour, a patterned rug.
round_27_fixes_checked.7 evidence: 250 m night supplied; game cutaway in a real colony and the follow view still missing.

apartment_block.identity: At 110 m and 250 m, day and night, it reads as the big housing building: a large stepped drum in three tiers with the house badge, glazed rings and a roof terrace; clearly different from the habitat dome and the tubes.
apartment_block.floors: Floor cutaway renders per floor show a ring of furnished units round a central lift and stair core; the top floor has penthouses with a wood terrace and two pools. Anchors per floor supplied.
apartment_block.faults: Floor 1's outer ring is a wide empty grey balcony band (about a third of the floor area); the upper-floor exterior is a plain grey drum with small windows (apartment_block_m_exterior) and needs balconies and lit windows to read as homes; at night the block's windows are few.

fixes.fix: Apartment block floor 1 outer ring: fill the empty band with private balconies per unit (a table, two chairs, planters) separated by screens, or shrink it to 1.5 m.
Apartment block exterior: a window per unit on every floor with warm light at night, balconies on floor 1, and the penthouse terrace visible from 110 m (pergola, pools lit at night).
Executive units: a second furniture set (upholstered bed, armchairs, a bookcase, art) so Executive differs by quality, not only by floor colour.
Night: a soft ceiling fill so rooms are not dim grey away from lamps (the V3 7.3 rule: no dark rooms).
Evidence for the final: in-game cutaway in a real colony, the apartment floor selector in game, the follow view in a family unit and a penthouse.

identity_test.110 m day: 3 of 5 certain: park (glass dome over green, heart badge), jail (fence ring on the roof, guard tower), academy (mast and dome). Retail and security are uncertain: retail carries the comfort heart like the lounge and the park; security shows the same blue shield as the jail.
identity_test.250 m day: 2 of 5: park and (by the fence) jail. Retail reads as the lounge; academy's atom badge reads as the research lab; security reads as the jail.
identity_test.250 m night: 2 of 5: the park glows green with lights; the rest are dark discs with small badges.

civic_modules.security_vs_jail: Not distinct enough. Both are the same flat grey drum with the same blue shield badge and blue band; at 250 m the only difference is a small tower and a thin fence rail that disappear at game size. V5 section 1 gives security black and red; use it. Give the jail its own badge and silhouette.
what_works: Park: the one green place, a glass geodesic dome over lawns, paths, trees, flower beds, a pond, benches; it glows at night.
Jail L: cells with bars in a ring round a guard post and a yard area; reads as serious but not grim.
Academy: rows of desks with chairs, a teacher board, instructor consoles.
Retail: clothing racks, mannequins, shelves, a counter, a café corner.

fixes.fix: Own badges: retail a shopping bag, academy a book or mortarboard, security a shield in black and red, jail barred window or a lock. Never reuse the comfort heart or the science atom for civic buildings.

Security vs jail silhouettes: security office a flat roof with a comms mast, a beacon and a black-and-red band; jail a raised perimeter wall with corner towers and floodlights round the roof and an orange band (prison orange). Each must read at 250 m without the badge.
Retail silhouette: shop-front awnings and lit signage round the drum, a billboard mast larger than now, and warm lit windows at night.

Empty floors: retail M/L, security office M, academy M and jail S leave 40-60% of the floor empty (the v4 1.5x scale). Fill by function: retail more shelf rows and a fitting room; security a briefing table, lockers, a monitor wall, a holding cell; academy a second class area, a library corner and a lab bench; jail S a yard strip and a visitor table.

Security office interior reads as a storeroom (scattered boxes on grey tile). Make it a command post: a raised desk facing a wall of monitors, a dispatch console, an armoury locker row, the black-and-red accent.
Night: all civic modules except the park are dark discs at 250 m. Lit windows in the band and a lit badge per module.

notes: civic_modules PASS 0.65, marginal and provisional: the park is good, but 3 of 5 modules do not pass the label-free identity test at 250 m and the floors are sparse.
Tone check: no child in the jail; nothing inappropriate.
